No change made — the `feat(domain): add domain length limit` commit is already right.

What I verified (by reading the code and exercising the regex with Node, since the sandbox is offline):

- The new pattern `/^(?=.{1,253}$)([a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\.)+[a-zA-Z]{2,}$/` in [regex.ts](~/muse_suggest/valibot__a0aa98555c__blind/repo/library/src/regex.ts:33) is exactly "old pattern AND length ≤ 253": a 200k-case fuzz over valid/invalid characters (including `\n`, `\r`, non-ASCII, emoji) found zero mismatches, and the `.`-doesn't-match-newline subtlety is irrelevant because any string containing such characters already fails the main pattern.
- 253 is the correct textual limit (255-octet wire format minus length/root bytes), and the passing test vector (`63.63.63.61`) is exactly the wire-maximum domain, with the `63.63.63.62` (254-char) case correctly rejected.
- The boundary tests in [domain.test.ts](~/muse_suggest/valibot__a0aa98555c__blind/repo/library/src/actions/domain/domain.test.ts:78) sit in the right suites, all labels respect the 63-char per-label rule, and `DOMAIN_REGEX` has no other consumers or conflicting tests.

One pre-existing observation, out of scope for this change: the TLD part `[a-zA-Z]{2,}` has no 63-char per-label cap (e.g. `'a.' + 'b'.repeat(64)` passes), but that predates this commit and is a separate issue from the total-length limit, so I left it untouched.
